records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed has no rescue around `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` or SimpleRSS.parse, and the job sets retry: false. A single transient DNS/timeout failure or a malformed feed body permanently kills that hour's poll with an unhandled exception and zero retries — feed import stops until the next scheduled run, with no verification or alerting that content was missed.
records.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then directly performs network/parse operations without any error handling: `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Both `open(...)` and `SimpleRSS.parse(...)` can raise exceptions (timeouts/DNS/invalid feed body). With no `rescue`, any such exception will abort that run and, because retries are disabled, Sidekiq will not retry the job for that scheduled execution, potentially missing imports until the next hourly run.

records.issue_text: [BUG] When an existing TopicEmbed's post_id points to a deleted/missing post, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError. A hard-deleted post (e.g., via a moderation cleanup that does not cascade to topic_embeds) makes every subsequent feed poll for that URL crash inside the job, and because update happens before embed.update_column, the embed row keeps pointing at the missing post forever with retry disabled.
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes the associated post exists: `post = embed.post` then `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `embed.post` is `nil` (e.g., orphaned `topic_embeds.post_id`), `PostRevisor#revise!` will dereference `@post` (`@post.acting_user = ...` in lib/post_revisor.rb), causing a `NoMethodError`. Also, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` happens after `revise!`, so on exception the embed row is not updated and remains broken, matching the finding’s “keeps pointing at the missing post forever” mechanism.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs that start with a literal '/', so protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png`) and relative paths without leading slash (`img/wat.jpg`) pass through unresolved. records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only links/images with `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` are rewritten (see `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and same for `src`). This means relative paths like `img/wat.jpg` or `./img/wat.jpg` are not converted to absolute URLs despite the comment “Convert any relative URLs to absolute”. Also, protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn...`) *do* match `start_with?('/')` and will be rewritten incorrectly to `#{prefix}/cdn...` because of `href.sub(/^\/+/,'')`, producing broken URLs. This is a verifiable correctness issue in the diff.

Any attacker who embeds a page whose origin contains the forum URL as a substring can drive `discourse-resize` messages at the iframe; the damage is limited to height manipulation (and a string e.data from legacy browsers is silently ignored), so it is a hardening gap rather than a data-loss path.
records.rationale: The finding reverses the substring check. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:migrate:redo, a restored database whose schema_migrations lost the row, or a partial-migration recovery) has top_topics silently dropped and rebuilt empty, losing all computed top-topic metrics data with no backup step.

In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which can cause data loss if the migration is re-run or if `top_topics` already exists for any reason. This is a real, verifiable risky behavior introduced by the diff and is unrelated to the embedding feature changes.

A hanging or slow feed URL blocks the scheduled job indefinitely; when open raises (DNS failure, 404, malformed feed), the exception is raised in a job with retries disabled and no logging call anywhere in the diff, so feed import silently stops forever with zero operator-visible signal.

records.issue_text: [BUG] In the update path, embed.post is used without a nil check; if the post has been deleted (or post_id dangles), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError. PollFeed or retrieve_topic crashes with NoMethodError on nil post inside the scheduled/retry:false job, aborting the whole remaining feed items for that run, and the embed page for that URL keeps showing the loading view indefinitely because no embed state ever changes.
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes the associated post exists: `post = embed.post` then `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `embed.post` is `nil` (e.g., orphaned `topic_embeds.post_id`), `PostRevisor#revise!` will dereference `@post` (`@post.acting_user = ...` in lib/post_revisor.rb), causing a `NoMethodError`. Also, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` happens after `revise!`, so on exception the embed row is not updated and remains broken, matching the finding’s “keeps pointing at the missing post forever” mechanism.

records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) runs unconditionally after revisor.revise!, even when the underlying @post.save fails its validations, so the hash is advanced while the write failed. A failed post revision is recorded as done: on every subsequent poll the content_sha1 comparison shows 'no change' and the revision is never re-attempted, so the post silently stays stale forever while the pipeline reports success.
records.rationale: The finding’s core mechanism hinges on a validation failure in the update path, but the diff shows validations are explicitly skipped. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller's contents string in place (contents << ...) before hashing and branching, so the same string passed twice gets the 'Imported from' footer appended twice. Any caller that reuses a content string across two imports (e.g. a future retry or the poll loop holding the item) silently accumulates duplicated footer HTML in the post body; also the raw caller-visible argument is mutated as a side effect.
records.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends the footer via an in-place mutation: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` before computing `content_sha1` and before branching on whether the embed exists. This mutates the caller-provided string object, so if the same `contents` string instance is reused across multiple calls (retry, repeated import, etc.), the footer will be appended multiple times, changing both the stored post body and the SHA used for change detection. The side effect on the argument is directly visible from the diff in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`.
